paper_metadata.title: Financial Fraud Detection with Entropy Computing

experiments.description: CVQBoost fraud-detection classification on the Kaggle credit card fraud dataset using Dirac-3 as the continuous-variable quadratic solver, evaluated against XGBoost under multiple class-balancing strategies and imbalance ratios.

algorithm.variant: CVQBoost with logistic-regression weak classifiers on Dirac-3

hyperparameters.weak_classifier_feature_count: one or two features per weak classifier

problem_formulation.objective_function: min_w sum_s |sum_i w_i h_i(x_s) - y_s|^2 + lambda * sum_i w_i^2, with w_i >= 0 and sum_i w_i = 1
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: continuous positive weights with an overall sum-to-one constraint; no binary encoding required
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: min_w sum_i sum_j J_ij w_i w_j + sum_i C_i w_i, where J_ij = sum_s h_i(x_s) h_j(x_s) + delta_ij lambda and C_i = -2 sum_s y_s h_i(x_s)

problem_instance.description: Credit card fraud detection on a highly imbalanced public benchmark dataset

dataset_specification.description: European credit card transactions over a two-day period in September 2013; approximately 0.1% fraudulent transactions; training data was rebalanced using ADASYN, SMOTE, SMOTE-SVM, or downsampling while test data remained unchanged; minority-to-majority ratios swept over 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.5, 1.0

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Class balancing applied only to training data; test set left unchanged
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: AUC on test data; results averaged over 10 runs

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Training-set class balancing via ADASYN, SMOTE, SMOTE-SVM, or downsampling; weak classifiers built from one or two features
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: AUC evaluation on unchanged test data
implementation_details.quantum_execution_time: Dirac-3 runtime reported separately from preprocessing/postprocessing
implementation_details.quantum_fraction_of_runtime: Dirac-3 component is a substantial portion of total CVQBoost runtime; exact fraction not reported

convergence_data.variance_across_runs: Reported as mean +/- standard deviation over 10 runs; error bars shown as two standard deviations

speedup_claims.factor: competitive accuracy; no speedup claimed for accuracy
speedup_claims.conditions: with class balancing applied; especially at higher minority-to-majority ratios
speedup_claims.caveats: At low imbalance ratios XGBoost has higher AUC; CVQBoost matches or exceeds XGBoost only when balancing is stronger.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Not explicitly stated; paper claims favorable/linear scaling of Dirac-3 runtime with problem size in experiments
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Not explicitly stated; XGBoost observed to scale faster than linearly with training size and roughly quadratically with feature count in the reported experiments
complexity_analysis.crossover_n: Around 20,000 training samples for the single-core XGBoost comparison; Dirac-3 also outperforms classical baselines at 900 Hamiltonian variables in the solver comparison
